text: Assumption 1 . For problem ( MI ), let $F$ be monotone and $L_{F}$ -Lipschitz. Assume that $r$ is proper, convex, closed. There exists $\mathbf{x}^{\star}$ such that $0\in(F+\partial r)(\mathbf{x}^{\star})$ . We have access to an unbiased estimator of $F$ such that $\mathbb{E}[F_{\xi}(\mathbf{x})]=F(\mathbf{x})$ .

Assumption 2 (Blum-Gladyshev variance) . Let the unbiased estimator of $F$ satisfy $\mathbb{E}\|F_{\xi}(\mathbf{x})-F(\mathbf{x})\|^{2}\leq B^{2}\|\mathbf{x}-\mathring{\mathbf{z}}\|^{2}+G^{2},$ where $\mathring{\mathbf{z}}$ is a fixed initial point. In view of Assumption 1 , denote $\widehat{L}_{F}=L_{F}+B$ .

Corollary 2.1 . For problem ( MI ), let Assumption 1 hold and suppose that Assumption 2 holds with $B=0$ . Additionally assume that $F$ is $\mu_{F}$ -strongly monotone. Let $S=\lfloor\log_{2}(L_{F}/\mu_{F})\rfloor\geq 1$ , $T\geq 48SL_{F}/\mu_{F}$ and $\eta=\frac{1}{3L_{F}}$ . Then, we have that $\mathbb{E}\|\mathcal{G}_{\eta,H}(\mathbf{z}_{S})\|\leq\varepsilon,$ (2.4) where the number of stochastic first-order oracles $T$ is upper bounded by $O\left(\frac{L_{F}}{\mu_{F}}\log\left(\frac{L_{F}}{\mu_{F}}\right)\log\left(\frac{\mu_{F}D_{\star}}{\varepsilon}+e\right)+\frac{G^{2}\log^{3}(L_{F}/\mu_{F})}{\varepsilon^{2}}\right).$ where $O$ only suppresses the absolute constants.

Corollary 2.2 . For problem ( MI ), let Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. We apply Algorithm 3 to solve ( 2.1 ) with $\mu=\frac{32\widehat{L}_{F}}{\sqrt{T}}\log_{2}^{3/2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{T}}{48}\right)$ , $T\geq 14175$ , $\eta=\frac{1}{3\widehat{L}_{F}}$ . Then, we have that $\mathbb{E}\|\mathcal{G}_{\eta,H}(\mathbf{z}_{S})\|=O\left(\frac{\widehat{L}_{F}D_{\star}(\ln\sqrt{T})^{3/2}}{\sqrt{T}}+\frac{(\ln\sqrt{T})^{5/2}(BD_{\star}+G)}{\sqrt{T}}\right).$ (2.6) Consequently, to obtain $\mathbb{E}\|\mathcal{G}_{\eta,H}(\mathbf{z}_{S})\|\leq\varepsilon,$ (2.7) the number of required stochastic first-order oracles $T$ is upper bounded by $O\left(1+\frac{(L_{F}^{2}+B^{2})D_{\star}^{2}+G^{2}}{\varepsilon^{2}}\ln^{5}\left(\frac{D_{\star}(L_{F}+B)+G}{\varepsilon}+1\right)\right),$ where we only suppress the absolute constants.

Assumption 3 . For problem ( 3.1 ), let $A$ be monotone, $L_{A}$ -Lipschitz and $\mu_{A}$ -strongly monotone. Assume that $r$ is proper, convex, closed. There exists $\mathbf{x}^{\star}_{A}$ such that $0\in(A+\partial r)(\mathbf{x}^{\star}_{A})$ . We have access to an unbiased estimator of $A$ such that $\mathbb{E}[A_{\xi}(\mathbf{x})]=A(\mathbf{x})$ and $\mathbb{E}\|A_{\xi}(\mathbf{x})-A(\mathbf{x})\|^{2}\leq B_{A}^{2}\|\mathbf{x}-\mathring{\mathbf{z}}\|^{2}+G_{A}^{2},$ where $\mathring{\mathbf{z}}$ is a globally fixed iterate.

Remark 3.2 . In this bound, the additional term $B^{2}_{A}\|\mathring{\mathbf{z}}-\mathbf{x}^{\star}_{A}\|^{2}$ coming from the relaxed variance requirement seems not problematic since $\mathbf{x}^{\star}_{A}$ is fixed. However, we will later invoke this result with a dynamic set of problems where the solution $\mathbf{x}^{\star}_{A}$ will be changing at each step. As a result, we cannot treat this term as a constant. We will have to craft a specialized analysis to handle this additional term since we do not have a global upper bound for the solutions of inner problems. This will be handled in Section 5 .

Theorem 4.3 . For problem ( MI ), let Assumption 1 hold and suppose that Assumption 2 holds with $B=0$ . Additionally assume that $F$ is $\mu_{F}$ strongly monotone for $\mu_{F}>0$ . We apply Algorithm 3 to solve ( 2.1 ) with $\eta=\frac{1}{3L_{F}}$ , $S=\lfloor\log_{2}(L_{F}/\mu_{F})\rfloor\geq 1$ and $T\geq 48SL_{F}/\mu_{F}$ , and initial point $\mathring{\mathbf{z}}$ . Then, we have that $\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\|\mathcal{G}_{\eta,H}(\mathbf{z}_{S})\|=O\left(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{T}{48SL_{F}/\mu_{F}}}\mu_{F}D_{\star}+\frac{S^{3/2}G}{\sqrt{T}}\right),$ where $O$ only suppresses the absolute constants.

Corollary 4.4 . Under the same setup as Theorem 4.3 , we have $\mathbb{E}\|\mathcal{G}_{\eta,H}(\mathbf{z}_{S})\|\leq\varepsilon,$ (4.5) where the number of stochastic first-order oracles $T$ is upper bounded by $O\left(\frac{L_{F}}{\mu_{F}}\log\left(\frac{L_{F}}{\mu_{F}}\right)\log\left(\frac{\mu_{F}D_{\star}}{\varepsilon}+e\right)+\frac{G^{2}\log^{3}(L_{F}/\mu_{F})}{\varepsilon^{2}}\right).$

Theorem 4.5 (Monotone $F$ ) . For problem ( MI ), let Assumption 1 hold and suppose that Assumption 2 holds with $B=0$ . We apply Algorithm 3 to solve ( 2.1 ) with any $L_{F}/2\geq\mu>0$ , $\eta=\frac{1}{3L_{F}}$ , $S=\lfloor\log_{2}(L_{F}/\mu)\rfloor\geq 1$ and $T\geq 48SL_{F}/\mu$ , and initial point $\mathring{\mathbf{z}}$ . Then, we have that $\mathbb{E}\|\mathcal{G}_{\eta,H}(\mathbf{z}_{S})\|=O\left(\mu\|\mathbf{x}^{\star}-\mathring{\mathbf{z}}\|+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{T}{48SL_{F}/\mu}}\mu\|\mathring{\mathbf{z}}-\mathbf{x}^{\star}\|+\frac{S^{3/2}G}{\sqrt{T}}\right).$

Corollary 4.6 . Under the same setup of Theorem 4.5 , let $T\geq 2200$ and $\mu=\frac{96L_{F}\log_{2}T}{T}$ . We apply Algorithm 3 to solve ( 2.1 ) with $\eta=\frac{1}{3L_{F}}$ , $S=\lfloor\log_{2}(L_{F}/\mu)\rfloor$ , and initial point $\mathring{\mathbf{z}}$ . Then, we have that $\mathbb{E}\|\mathcal{G}_{\eta,H}(\mathbf{z}_{S})\|=O\left(\frac{L_{F}D_{\star}\log_{2}T}{T}+\frac{G(\log_{2}T)^{3/2}}{\sqrt{T}}\right).$ (4.7) Consequently, to obtain $\mathbb{E}\|\mathcal{G}_{\eta,H}(\mathbf{z}_{S})\|\leq\varepsilon,$ (4.8) the required number of stochastic first-order oracles $T$ is upper bounded by $O\left(1+\frac{L_{F}D_{\star}}{\varepsilon}\ln\left(\frac{L_{F}D_{\star}}{\varepsilon}+1\right)+\frac{G^{2}}{\varepsilon^{2}}\ln^{3}\left(\frac{G}{\varepsilon}+1\right)\right),$ where we only suppress the absolute constants.

Theorem 5.2 . For problem ( MI ), let Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. We apply Algorithm 3 to solve ( 2.1 ) with $\mu=\frac{32\widehat{L}_{F}}{\sqrt{T}}\log_{2}^{3/2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{T}}{48}\right),~~~\eta=\frac{1}{3\widehat{L}_{F}},~~~S=\lfloor\log_{2}(\widehat{L}_{F}/\mu)\rfloor,~~~T\geq 14175,$ and initial point $\mathring{\mathbf{z}}$ . Then, we have that $\mathbb{E}\|\mathcal{G}_{\eta,H}(\mathbf{z}_{S})\|=O\left(\mu D_{\star}+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{T}{48S\widehat{L}_{F}/\mu}}\mu D_{\star}+\frac{S^{5/2}\left(BD_{\star}+G\right)}{\sqrt{T}}\right).$

Remark 5.3 . By the value of $\mu=\widetilde{O}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\right)$ and $T\geq 48S\widehat{L}_{F}/\mu$ as shown in Lemma 6.7 , one can estimate that the complexity will be of the order $\varepsilon^{-2}$ up to logarithmic terms. We follow by a corollary for the order of the terms and then we give the precise constants.

Corollary 5.4 . Under the same setup of Theorem 5.2 , with $\mu=\frac{32\widehat{L}_{F}}{\sqrt{T}}\log_{2}^{3/2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{T}}{48}\right)$ , $T\geq 14175$ , we have that $\mathbb{E}\|\mathcal{G}_{\eta,H}(\mathbf{z}_{S})\|=O\left(\frac{\widehat{L}_{F}D_{\star}(\ln\sqrt{T})^{3/2}}{\sqrt{T}}+\frac{(\ln\sqrt{T})^{5/2}(BD_{\star}+G)}{\sqrt{T}}\right).$ (5.13) Consequently, to obtain $\mathbb{E}\|\mathcal{G}_{\eta,H}(\mathbf{z}_{S})\|\leq\varepsilon,$ (5.14) the number of required stochastic first-order oracles $T$ is upper bounded by $O\left(1+\frac{(L_{F}^{2}+B^{2})D_{\star}^{2}+G^{2}}{\varepsilon^{2}}\ln^{5}\left(\frac{D_{\star}(L_{F}+B)+G}{\varepsilon}+1\right)\right),$ where we only suppress the absolute constants.

Fact 6.5 . Let $F$ satisfy Assumption 2 with constants $B,G$ . Then, $F^{s}$ defined in ( 2.3 ), satisfies the BG assumption with the same constants. Moreover, $F^{s-1}$ is $(L_{F}+(2^{s}-1)\mu)$ -Lipschitz, $((2^{s}-1)\mu)$ -strongly monotone.
